chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Rex Stewart and Freddie Hubbard
summary: Hubbard's trumpet reminds Collins of Rex Stewart, another reason young players should go back and listen.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. I heard the trumpet players now doing Freddy Hubbard and a lot of the things that he does reminds me of Rex Stewart. You see, Rex Stewart was a great trumpet player, he was an innovator, you know, and a lot of the things that the trumpet players are doing now, and especially Freddy Hubbard, reminds me of what Rex Stewart was doing then. And I'm sure that Freddy's probably aware of this, you know, but so much of this has been done that the average student or young musicians now aren't aware of. And I think they should be, whatever their particular instrument is, you know. They should kind of dig back and -- delve back and see where it came from. And it'll be so enlightening, and beneficial to them.
